items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-10-26
items.q: Marshall Stern founded a good racket. He got any milk. The Guggenheimer Foundation on it. Got a lot of money.

ctx.x: Maybe I'll get in trouble by mentioning Edgar Stein but he put money in there. But this Edgar Stein had a lot to do from keeping me from getting recognition because he was a big owner in the times, picking on a long time ago. And I found out all this stuff, not recently, but in a roundabout way, things have been rounding themselves up. this Dave Stein came here, he bought the New Orleans item in. He was the same man who created the talking mule, Francis. He helped to create the talking jackasses, the New Orleans…

Aided in a better by no other than Dr. Sushant, who puts himself as a jazz historian. Now this man here, as a jazz historian, never played jazz. He says he used to sit across the road from on Basin Street and listen to Joe Oliver playing music. And there's where he got his idea from. Well now the only thing he could have heard on Basin Street, and there's many more men as old as I am, can tell you they had no music on Basin Street outside a little violin or a piano. Or they had three Negro Rhymers at Anderson's.…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: Marshall Stern, self-appointed prophet of jazz music, mocked

ctx.x: The reason I wrote them, I thought they would make them give me the same time that these dirty low-down people put this program on, that I would have the same time as an American citizen to tell them my side of the story. But the Federal Radio Commission seemed different. I had to sue them. Well, now I had to try to get that script first. There's my letter to WDSU. Would you read that? All right.

All right. All right. All right. All right. You guys in? Yes, this is a letter from D. James, Nick LaRocca, 2218 Constant Street, New Orleans, Louisiana, 13, January 13, 1957. Mr. Swayze, manager, WDSU television station, 520 Royal Street City. Dear Mr. Swayze, the purpose of this letter is to request of you a script on a program. Read the supposed history of jazz as told through the facilities of WDDU. WDSU. WDSU. WDSU by Armand Hull and one of your announcers. This program happened around August of 1955. This…
No, no. That was added after.
